sections.html:
The quickest routes are a cash sale or an as-is sale to an investor, since neither waits on a mortgage approval. A standard listing still makes sense for a house in good shape, though it brings showings, an appraisal and the buyer's loan timeline.

Walla Walla is the seat of Walla Walla County, in a valley of southeastern Washington about 6 miles north of the Oregon line. The city is compact, around 13 square miles, and sits beside College Place, which adds a second small city to the same housing market.

The median home is valued at $393,600 and 57.1 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. The population is nearly flat at 34,058, down 0.6 percent from the 2020 base, so buyers will compare your house closely against others for sale instead of assuming rising demand will lift it. The average commute is under 13 minutes, which is a real asset when you describe the location.

sections.h2: Design numbers for repairs and additions
sections.html:
Walla Walla sits in the Cascades' rain shadow, so rainfall is modest, but winters can still turn cold. Anything you repair or add has to meet the city's building design numbers, which are published by Development Services:

  • Ground and minimum roof snow load of 30 pounds per square foot
  • Design wind speed of 110 mph
  • Seismic design category D
  • Frost depth of 24 inches
  • Ice shield underlayment required

If you replaced a roof or built a structure, keep the permit paperwork to hand over at closing. A buyer's inspector often asks for it.

Most of the city is in Walla Walla Public Schools, with seven elementary schools, two middle schools, one traditional high school (Wa-Hi) and two alternative high schools, Lincoln and Opportunity. The far western edge belongs to the College Place School District. Private options include Walla Walla Catholic Schools and several Christian schools.

U.S. Route 12 is the main east-west highway, and State Route 125 runs through town into Milton-Freewater, Oregon. Valley Transit serves Walla Walla and College Place and has been fare-free since 2022. The regional airport has commercial flights to Seattle-Tacoma twice a day.

If the job is structural, mechanical or plumbing, Development Services handles the permit. The department issues permits and inspections for new construction, remodels, mechanical and plumbing work, signs and other land use activity inside city limits, and it adopted the 2021 International Building Codes.

Applications, payments and inspection requests are now online for permits processed after August 19, 2025. Older permits may still involve calls to the permit technicians for payment and inspections. For a project that is not clearly covered, ask Development Services before you start. Work done without a required permit can turn up in a buyer's inspection, so it is cheaper to sort out beforehand than during escrow.

The rules depend on which type of short-term rental you have. A Type 1 rental is the owner's principal residence, either with rooms rented while the owner is present or the entire dwelling rented no more than 90 days a year. A Type 2 rental is a dwelling that is not the owner's principal residence.

Ordinance 2017-33 bans new Type 2 rentals. Those lawfully operating before November 9, 2017 may continue as non-conforming uses, and that status runs with the property as long as the use has not been abandoned. A buyer of such a property must obtain a Type 2 permit and license at closing, with proof of ownership. The permit can be lost in several ways:

  • Use is presumed abandoned if the location was not rented at least a total of 29 days in the preceding year
  • Use ends if the location sits unrented for 6 consecutive months or more
  • A fourth nuisance violation leads to revocation, after fines of $750 and then $1,000

If you own a Type 2 rental, ask Development Services for the current permit status before you advertise, since a buyer's offer may depend on it.

sections.h2: How the deed and excise tax work
sections.html:
The real estate excise tax goes to the treasurer of the county where the property sits, who acts as the state's agent under RCW 82.45.090. The county auditor cannot take the deed for recording until payment is verified or the treasurer notes that nothing is due. In Walla Walla County that means the Treasurer first, then recording through the Auditor.

The tax combines a state portion and a local portion, so ask the County Treasurer for the total at your sale price. A title or escrow company normally carries the affidavit and deed through both offices.

You also owe the buyer a written condition disclosure. RCW 64.06.020 prescribes the form for improved residential property and sets delivery at five business days after a signed contract, unless the parties agree otherwise. Receiving it gives the buyer three business days to back out.

Start by deciding which kind of buyer suits your house. A cash buyer or investor takes a house with deferred maintenance and does not wait on a lender. A conventional buyer will expect the repairs to be done or priced in.

Then gather what any buyer will ask for: permit paperwork for roofs and additions, the status of a short-term rental permit if you have one, and the excise tax figure from the Treasurer. Known defects and unpermitted work belong on the disclosure form. Getting this ready first keeps a cash sale quick and keeps a listing from stalling after an offer.

When offers arrive, compare them on what you net after repairs and carrying costs, who pays the excise tax, and the closing date. A cash buyer skips the appraisal and loan approval, so the closing date is mostly a matter of title work and your own move. Ask a title or escrow company to confirm the payoff before you sign anything, and keep a copy of every document you hand over. If the house has a tenant or stored belongings, agree in writing on what stays and when the place will be empty.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Walla Walla house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Investors and cash buyers often take houses with deferred maintenance. The seller disclosure under RCW 64.06.020 still goes to the buyer, and known defects or unpermitted work belong on it.

faqs.q: Can a new owner keep running my Walla Walla house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Only in limited cases. New Type 2 rentals are banned, but a lawfully established one that has not been abandoned keeps its non-conforming status with the property. The new owner must obtain a Type 2 permit and license at closing with proof of ownership.

faqs.q: What building design numbers apply to Walla Walla houses?
faqs.a: A 30 pound per square foot roof snow load, a 110 mph wind speed, seismic design category D and a 24 inch frost depth, plus ice shield underlayment. These apply to new work under the 2021 International Building Codes.

faqs.q: Who collects the excise tax when a Walla Walla house sells?
faqs.a: The county treasurer, acting as the state's agent under RCW 82.45.090. Recording waits until the tax is paid or noted as not due, so ask the Walla Walla County Treasurer for the figure at your price.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Walla Walla address?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Walla Walla Public Schools, and the extreme western edge is in the College Place School District. Confirm the boundary with the district for your street.
